## Static compatibility regression in PR #189
Exact reviewed head: `2d83808dd35ba96a19406deca49373976048d073`, compared with `75acc52aa905db1aee0c5f694f05d16b86e49c4b`.

The new forward-only importer is documented honestly: earlier successful items remain applied, per-item conflicts/uncertain outcomes are reported, and SDK read-to-write limitations are disclosed. This issue is **not** a request to weaken those safeguards or restore unsafe rollback.

The compatibility problem is that existing callers still explicitly request the former atomic contract:
- CLI accepts `--atomic` on import/sync; its new help calls it a deprecated compatibility flag.
- [`SyncOptions.atomic`](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-linear/blob/2d83808dd35ba96a19406deca49373976048d073/index.ts#L2691-L2695) and [`importLinearAtomic`](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-linear/blob/2d83808dd35ba96a19406deca49373976048d073/index.ts#L3370-L3395) remain callable.
- The latter now invokes the forward-only coordinator and returns `recovered:false` plus a descriptive `linear-forward-…` transactionId, not a durable recovery journal.
- [Coordinator](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-linear/blob/2d83808dd35ba96a19406deca49373976048d073/index.ts#L2774-L2925) applies native writes, retains prior successes after later failure, and reports `atomic:false`. Reporting the changed guarantee after writes is too late for an existing caller that explicitly requested the old mode.
- Previously injectable batch commit seams are retained but inert; source/type compatibility is not behavioral compatibility.

## Existing documented contract
[Canonical pm-linear-nvt5](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-linear/blob/2d83808dd35ba96a19406deca49373976048d073/.agents/pm/tasks/pm-linear-nvt5.toon), delivered by [PR #36](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-linear/pull/36), explicitly records opt-in batch compensation and durable same-transaction recovery. This is the prior intended API contract, **not proof that old implementation supplied isolation against ordinary writers**; core #1576/#1620 limitations remain real.

PR189's feature tracker reports a fleet directive toward forward-only operations. A separately accepted public migration decision overriding the explicit atomic-request contract was not verified by this review. The concrete request here is a safe compatibility boundary, independent of whether forward-only becomes the chosen default.

## Expected vs actual / impact
When a caller requests an unavailable stronger guarantee, fail before native mutations with a typed, actionable migration response, or provide that guarantee using supported shared SDK semantics. Do not silently interpret `--atomic` / the atomic-named SDK entrypoint as permission for partial forward-only application.

Example existing workflow: import A and B with explicit atomic mode; B fails after A is applied. Under the new coordinator A intentionally stays applied. The caller must explicitly choose that tradeoff **before** writes, not discover it from the receipt.

The exported descriptive-fingerprint JSDoc also still says a reordered retry resumes a durable journal after adding a new non-executable-fingerprint disclaimer. Remove contradictory journal promises from the public helper documentation.

## Evidence and limits
Static exact-source analysis and canonical record comparison. A bounded independent extraction of the exact coordinator passed 200 in-memory mocked scenarios /919 assertions, including retention of earlier writes, truthful unconfirmed/reconciled outcomes, dependency skips and omitted unchanged status. SDK/graph/read/write behavior was mocked; this is **not** a native atomic/rollback/concurrency reproduction. Current exact-head full CI was queued at review. No provider calls, native writes, lock/security probes or release actions were performed.

All-status issues/PRs and linked canonical records checked; no separate compatibility/migration issue found. PR189 remains implementation owner.

## Acceptance
1. Preserve a supported explicit atomic guarantee through reusable SDK primitives, **or** reject deprecated atomic requests before any mutation and require an explicit forward-only migration choice. Do not claim transaction isolation that the SDK cannot provide.
2. Cover CLI aliases, `SyncOptions.atomic:true`, and `importLinearAtomic`; tests assert no mutation occurs when the requested guarantee is unavailable.
3. Preserve the forward-only mode's truthful applied/skipped/unconfirmed receipts, prior successes, full history and foreign-write protections.
4. Clearly distinguish descriptive receipt IDs from resumable transaction IDs; remove obsolete recovery/JSDoc promises and document source/API migration.
5. Record the accepted capability tradeoff and validate packed consumers and supported SDK versions without weakening guards or merely changing old atomic assertions to accept partial writes.
